subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: For iid observations with variance σ², Var(sample mean) is
solution_latex: Variance of the average is nσ²/n²=σ²/n.
common_mistake: Standard error is σ/√n; variance is its square.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: The Central Limit Theorem primarily says that
options: a standardized sum tends toward normality
variance becomes zero at finite n
solution_latex: Under suitable conditions, the centered and scaled sum converges in distribution to standard normal.
common_mistake: The population distribution itself does not change.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: If sample size is multiplied by 4, standard error is
solution_latex: Standard error is proportional to 1/√n.
common_mistake: It follows a square-root law.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: The law of large numbers concerns
options: convergence of sample mean to μ
solution_latex: The sample average stabilizes near the population mean as n grows.
common_mistake: LLN is about convergence, not fluctuation shape.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: For iid Xi with variance 9, Var(sum of 10 Xi) is
solution_latex: Independence makes variances add: 10·9=90.
common_mistake: Do not divide by n for a sum.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: Which condition is central to the classical iid CLT?
solution_latex: Finite variance supports the classical CLT; normal raw data and zero mean are unnecessary.
common_mistake: Thirty is a heuristic, not a theorem condition.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: For iid data with finite variance, which are true?
options: sample mean is exactly normal for every population and n
solution_latex: The first two follow directly and standard error shrinks. Exact finite-n normality is not universal.
common_mistake: CLT normality is generally approximate.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: If the original population is normal, the sample mean is
solution_latex: Linear combinations of independent normals are exactly normal.
common_mistake: No large-sample approximation is needed.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: A continuity correction is used when approximating
options: a discrete count by a continuous normal
solution_latex: A 0.5 boundary shift aligns discrete bars with continuous area.
common_mistake: It addresses discrete-to-continuous boundaries.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: Consistency informally means an estimator
options: gets close to the target as n grows
solution_latex: A consistent estimator concentrates around the true value.
common_mistake: Consistency is asymptotic and distinct from unbiasedness.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: Population SD is 15 and n=25. Enter standard error of the mean.
common_mistake: Use square root of sample size.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: iid variables have mean 4 and variance 9. For n=20, enter E[sum Xi].
solution_latex: Expectation of the sum is 20·4=80.
common_mistake: Means add linearly.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: For the same variables and n=20, enter Var(sum Xi).
solution_latex: Independence gives 20·9=180.
common_mistake: Sum variance multiplies by n.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: Population variance is 16 and n=64. Enter Var(sample mean).
solution_latex: Variance of the mean is 16/64=0.25.
common_mistake: This asks variance, not standard error.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: The standardized mean is (sample mean−50)/(10/√100). If sample mean=52, enter z.
solution_latex: The standard error is 1, so z=2.
common_mistake: Use sampling SD, not population SD alone.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: To reduce a standard error from 4 to 2, by what factor must n increase?
solution_latex: Halving error requires quadrupling n.
common_mistake: Precision follows a square-root law.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: For iid Bernoulli(0.3) data, enter E[sample mean].
solution_latex: The sample proportion is unbiased for p, so its mean is 0.3.
common_mistake: Averaging does not change expectation.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: For n=100 Bernoulli(0.3) data, enter 1000Var(sample mean).
solution_latex: Variance is 0.3·0.7/100=0.0021; scaling gives 2.1.
common_mistake: Use p(1−p)/n.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: A sum has variance 1600. Enter its standard deviation.
solution_latex: Standard deviation is √1600=40.
common_mistake: Take the square root of variance.

subject: probability-statistics
question_latex: If Z=(sample mean−μ)/(σ/√n) and sample mean=μ, enter Z.
solution_latex: The numerator is zero.
